pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: GRADE APPROPRIATE FICTION MATERIALS - CHARACTER

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: why. 1. What makes reading enjoyable?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the characters in a given fiction text
2. describe the traits of a given character in a fictional text

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify the characters in a given fiction text
   In simple words: practise until you can identify the characters in a given fiction text. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. describe the traits of a given character in a fictional text
   In simple words: practise until you can describe the traits of a given character in a fictional text. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character.
4. Show that you can: identify the characters in a given fiction text

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read a given fiction material on African heroes/heroines and list the characters in the text,
2. Role play the different characters identified,
3. Choose a character and discuss what the character does or says,
4. Creativity and imagination: It is developed and networking is enhanced as the learner role plays different characters.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. why. 1. What makes reading enjoyable?
2. How can the characters in a story be described?
3. Which stories are the most enjoyable to read?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify the characters in a given fiction text
2. describe the traits of a given character in a fictional text

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
